key_insight: A Neural Spline Flow can learn a smooth, invertible domain map so PDEs on complex geometries can be solved by pulling the problem back to a fixed reference mesh.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the need for repeated unstructured meshing and enables reusable, structured finite element workflows with potential gains in assembly efficiency, memory access, and quadrature reuse.
method: Use monotone rational-quadratic spline coupling layers to enforce a strictly positive Jacobian determinant.
Transfer the PDE weak form to a reference domain via a diffeomorphic pullback and solve with standard finite elements.
Condition a shared NSF on latent shape codes and predict those codes for new geometries with an encoder.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical benchmarks showing that sufficiently accurate learned mappings produce reliable finite element solutions.
watch_item: Overall accuracy depends on geometric fidelity, so mapping error must be controlled separately from discretization and quadrature error.
paper_title: Neural Spline Flow Diffeomorphisms for Pullback Finite Element Methods on Complex Domains
